observed: R1420 preserves ordinary decoder text and relocations, but the inline VEX32 reader causes frame setup on ineligible 64-bit paths. R1424 moves the call and removes most extra instruction cost, but changes ordinary text size and thousands of linked symbol positions; it fails native x86 and mixed-architecture timing gates.
hypothesis: Retain the R1420 callsite and all plan bytes. Split its wrapper into an eligibility-only selector and a separate same-signature plan leaf. Both selector branches forward the original arguments as tail calls; only the eligible leaf needs reader temporaries.
semantic_invariant: Same exact-mode, extension, extent and prefix guards; unchanged plan tables, reader, complete-result writes and canonical generic fallback.
lowering_gate: Require original ordinary text, function sizes/positions and relocations identical except the existing verified generic-call target. Inspect selector disassembly for stack/frame and actual tail transfers, then require full-record equivalence and retained native controls.
